methodological_rigor.justification: The study employs a custom MITO CRISPR library (1,083 mitochondrial genes, 4 sgRNAs each) screened in patient-derived PATC PDAC cell lines with modified BAGEL (Low Fat BAGEL), cross-referenced against multiple scoring methods (DEseq2, MAGeCK, SgRSEA, EdgeR, Z-ratio). Functional validation includes sgRNA and shRNA knockdown, mitochondrial OCR (Seahorse XFe96), MitoSOX ROS detection, mtDNA cytosolic release quantification by qPCR, cGAS-STING-IFN pathway Western blots, syngeneic KPC orthotopic and subcutaneous models in C57BL/6 and CD8 KO mice, anti-PD-1 combination, STING antagonist H-151 rescue, CD8 depletion rescue, IncuCyte proliferation monitoring. Exceptionally rigorous multi-model validation with genetic and pharmacological rescue experiments.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical study with patient-derived xenografts, syngeneic mouse models, and cell lines - Oxford LoE 5. Clinical translational relevance is strong because PDAC is immunologically cold with no effective immune checkpoint blockade response. Identifying GFER as a druggable target that both disrupts tumor redox balance and activates cGAS-STING-IFN-I-mediated immunogenicity, sensitizing to anti-PD-1, directly addresses a major therapeutic gap. The MITO CRISPR library framework is also a resource for the community.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods are detailed with IRB protocol ID (LAB07-0854), IACUC approval, specific catalog numbers for all reagents and antibodies, sgRNA/shRNA sequences, dosing regimens (anti-PD-1 100 μg every 3 days for 7 doses, H-151 750 nmol IP, anti-CD8 10 mg/kg). Mouse strain numbers (Jackson Laboratory) specified. Sample size justification based on prior literature. Randomization described; immunofluorescence analysis blinded though in vivo assessments not blinded - a limitation explicitly acknowledged. Aligns well with ARRIVE principles.

novelty_literature.justification: Identifies GFER (a mitochondrial FAD-dependent sulfhydryl oxidase with roles in Fe-S cluster transport) as a novel PDAC dependency through unbiased CRISPR screening of 1,083 mitochondrial genes. The dual mechanism whereby GFER depletion disrupts redox homeostasis AND releases mtDNA to activate cGAS-STING-IFN-I - converting cold PDAC to hot and sensitizing to anti-PD-1 - is a conceptually novel therapeutic strategy for an immunotherapy-resistant tumor type. The H-151 STING antagonist rescue experiment provides strong mechanistic evidence.

writing_presentation.justification: Abstract is duplicated (formatting artifact). Manuscript has clear logical progression from unbiased screen to mechanism (redox, mtDNA release) to immune consequences (cGAS-STING, T-cell infiltration) to therapeutic translation (anti-PD-1 combination). Methods are exceptionally detailed. Figures likely comprehensive with screen, biochemistry, and in vivo data.

key_strengths: Unbiased custom MITO CRISPR library (1,083 genes) identifying GFER as a context-specific PDAC vulnerability with multiple orthogonal bioinformatic scoring methods
Dual-mechanism discovery: GFER depletion disrupts mitochondrial redox balance AND releases mtDNA activating cGAS-STING-IFN-I pathway

Comprehensive in vivo validation across PDX (nude mice), syngeneic KPC (C57BL/6), and immune-deficient (CD8 KO) models with CD8 depletion, STING antagonist (H-151), and anti-PD-1 combination rescue experiments
Direct therapeutic demonstration: GFER depletion + anti-PD-1 enhances antitumor efficacy in immunocompetent model
Patient-derived xenograft models (PATC108, 124, 148) provide clinical relevance
key_concerns: Duplicated abstract is a formatting/editorial issue
GFER small-molecule inhibitor not available; dependency validated only through genetic approaches (sgRNA, shRNA, inducible doxycycline)
In vivo investigators were not blinded to treatment allocation as acknowledged
Sample sizes in some subgroups (n=3-10 mice) are modest; power calculations not explicitly reported
Translation from mouse to human will require druggability assessment and toxicity profiling not addressed
chief_reviewer.rationale: High-quality preclinical target discovery study with unbiased CRISPR screen, mechanistic depth (redox + cGAS-STING), and compelling combination therapy rescue of immune checkpoint resistance in PDAC, fitting Tier 2 (Cancer Discovery / Nature Cancer-caliber) with minor revisions.
